label: contract-audit-1
tail:
Both detectors pass, and no item file was touched.

## Adjudication

`citation-fidelity` printed **no candidates** on first run (exit 0, 1176 citations over 324 items). The entire candidate list was two `boundary-audit` rows, both on `fs-the-kleisli-and-eilenberg-moore-categories-are-equivalent-for-every-monad` — `iff-forward` and `iff-reverse`.

**Both are detector false positives. Upheld on the record, with a distinct reason each.**

- **iff-forward** — the `\bare equivalent\b` regex matched "categories are equivalent". `def-equivalence-and-adjoint-equivalence-of-categories.md:35` reads *"The categories are then called **equivalent**"*, so the phrase names a defined categorical predicate (quasi-inverses plus natural isomorphisms), not a biconditional. The Statement is one universally quantified claim under refutation — no antecedent/consequent for a forward direction to run between.
- **iff-reverse** — upheld on separate grounds, since the forward reason doesn't settle it. The one genuine iff in play is cited `[L3]` (`thm-fully-faithful-split-essentially-surjective-characterises-equivalence`), which lives in Facts & Assumptions as a quoted dependency, and step 3.1 uses only its forward direction. A one-directional use of someone else's biconditional owes no converse.

I did not rest the upholds on the tool's own header comment anticipating this case — I checked the definition file, and I verified the counterexample itself is sound (Kleisli endo-collections are 1 or infinite; `Mon({1,e},{1,e})` is exactly 2; the EM category is isomorphic *over Set* to Mon, so cardinalities transfer exactly). No confirmed defect, so **no defect-ledger row** — there is nothing real to record.

## Two things beyond the printed candidates

**A wider net over batch 7 found no defect the detector missed.** Six more items trip a broader biconditional test than `exhibitsIff` uses; five carry `checked` iff rows with real per-item step evidence, and the sixth (`thm-a-monadic-functor-is-conservative`) is honestly `not_applicable` — `def-conservative-functor` defines *conservative* **as** reflecting isomorphisms, so its "equivalently" is a definitional restatement, not an iff.

**One thing I left, deliberately and on the record:** 70 rows in batch 7 (zero elsewhere) share the tail *"…is a one-way theorem or computation; adding a forward/reverse half would create a biconditional absent from its Statement."* They escape `--fail-on-template` because `normalise` doesn't strip the varying subject phrase that opens each sentence. On the evidence this is style, not the frontier-13 concealed-defect class — the claim those rows make is precisely what `exhibitsIff` independently tests across all 70, and my wider re-test found nothing. I did not rewrite them: it's outside the candidate list, it's 70 genuine per-item reads rather than a sweep, and varying the wording with no finding behind it would be weakening a rationale to satisfy a regex. Flagged for the lead Alpha.

I also read `[L2]`'s *"is the category of monoids"* against the source's *"isomorphic over Set to the category of monoids"* and judged the elision faithful — the proof uses only the hom-set correspondence an isomorphism supplies — so I left it rather than void the contract row.

Files changed: the two `reviewed` blocks in `research/frontier-15-batch-7.proof-contracts.json`, the re-merged `research/frontier-15-proof-contracts.json` (verified both blocks survived the merge, so nothing comes back stale), and the report at `research/frontier-15-alpha-contract-audit.md`.
